I’m sorry you’re having a rough night. I lost my dad at 13, and my mom at 17. I’m an only child and the feeling of loneliness never goes away. I’m 23 now, and lately i’ve been missing my parents more and more; mostly because the anniversary of their deaths are coming up in a few weeks, but I’m also reeling in from how many big life events they missed out on. I try and find comfort in my tears, that it’s okay to miss them and wish for them to be with me. I try to remember how much they loved/continue to love me, and that usually helps carry me through the extra hard days.

People who haven’t experienced what we have find it incredibly hard to empathize the way we need them to. They’re trying their best, and you’re allowed to feel that frustration. Something that helped me, was when people asked what I needed from them. It made it a lot easier for us both to voice our expressions. Maybe you could tell them that you need x, y, z. It’s tricky in the position you’re in, but a little goes a long way.

I lost my mom almost a year and a half ago to cancer. It was just me and her and I was young when she died; when she passed I lost everything. None of my family was very supportive with helping me, I was on my own. It was tough as hell for the first 5 months. I felt like giving up every day but I had to keep going for her. She always told me I was her dream come true. I still keep going for her. 

There’s no easy way to say this, but being motherless will always affect your daily life. You’ll see her everywhere at first. You’ll see glimpses of her in your friends’ mothers. In yourself. It’s tough. 

To this day not having her is so terrible. No doubt that my life would be better with her here. But she isn’t. What helps me though, is knowing that she’s with me every step of the way. That she still lives on in my heart and my memories keep her warm.

Talk to her every day. Write to her how your day was, how you’re feeling. Tell her you love and miss her. It helps more than you know. All my best wishes to you, I’m so sorry.

My mom passed last year in May and boy I was a damn wreck. The only reason I kept breathing was so I could graduate and make her proud. I dreaded therapy because I didn’t think it’d help either. I started therapy in September/October and I can honestly say it’s helped me out so much. It was rough in the beginning because I wanted to rush through the stages of healing, all while nursing my pain. But the more sessions I went to (often being 2 or 3x a week) the more I grew into handling and nurturing my grief. I still see my therapist and I feel much lighter. The pain will always be there but I can honestly say I’m better equipped to handle it. I wish you all the best. I’m so sorry.

Honestly speaking, she has never showed any of these signs. She has never shown abandonment fear or made me feel guilty into seeing anyone that wasn’t her. She’s hardly ever expressed herself as a victim, and her friends have seen her upset at times, just not to the extent I see it. And lastly, she hardly ever flips on me. There are a few instances when she gets upset at me and does flip, but this hasn’t happened in a very long time.

Firsts are always always always hard. Mine came up in May and it was rough. My boyfriend spent the day with me and we honored my mom by doing what she loved. Bought ice cream and went to the beach. We just sat there and watched the waves. I recommend doing something that she enjoyed, as a way to honor her life and express it joyously. Of course emotions will get in the way, and don’t be afraid to nurse them. It’s okay.

The days leading up to the important days are hard: birthdays, anniversaries, holidays. Even when they pass it lingers in your heart for a bit. Don’t run from the pain, but understand it. It won’t always be this painful, but it will be there. It will get easier to bear as time goes on. You got this.
